type.description: Error category. Generic: REQUEST_NOT_VALID, UNAUTHORIZED, FORBIDDEN, RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND, RESOURCE_CONFLICT, UNPROCESSABLE, INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR; or a domain type (see code).

code.description: String. Generic 10400/10401/10403/10404/10409/10422/10500, or a domain code documented for this endpoint: 501422 RATE_UNAVAILABLE_ERROR, 213400 UNSUPPORTED_CURRENCY_PAIRS.

gotchas: Auth: one token server for both environments — the docs' Multi-Environment Integrations example sends either environment's credentials to https://idp.flutterwave.com/realms/flutterwave/protocol/openid-connect/token, and Authentication says "This process applies to both the sandbox and production environments. Make sure to use the correct credentials for each environment to obtain a valid token." "Each token is valid for **10 minutes**"; "We recommend refreshing the token at least one minute before it expires." Cache the token. Sandbox: "We archive your test data after 30 days."

Headers: send X-Idempotency-Key on this POST. Docs (Idempotency): "For all `POST` endpoints, include an idempotency key in the request header (`X-Idempotency-Key`)." The API reference marks it optional; the headers guide lists it under 'Mandatory API Headers'. A reused key replays the first response ("the response will include the header `X-Idempotency-Cache-Hit: true`"), so reuse the key when retrying the same operation and use a new one for a new operation. X-Trace-Id is optional. For both: "It must be a string using only alphanumeric ASCII characters." "Its length should be between 12 and 255 characters." The idempotency page also says "We recommend using a **UUID** string as your idempotency key": strip the UUID's hyphens to satisfy both.

The quote does not lock the rate: Docs (Real-time FX conversion): "Fetching the live exchange rate is optional. Flutterwave automatically uses real-time rates when you start a transfer." create_transfer takes no rate id. The rate actually used is in the transfer's debit_information.
Body: source {currency}, destination {currency, amount}, optional precision (2-9, default 6). The response gives the source amount needed for the destination amount.
Limits apply to the converted amount: Docs (Transfer Orchestrator): "If the converted amount exceeds or falls below the allowed limits for the destination currency, the transfer will fail."

Errors: {"status":"failed","error":{"type","code","message","validation_errors"}}; error.code is a string and 400s carry validation_errors[{field_name,message}]. Besides the generic codes (10400 REQUEST_NOT_VALID, 10401, 10403 FORBIDDEN, 10404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND, 10409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT, 10422 UNPROCESSABLE, 10500) the error table documents these for this endpoint: 501422 RATE_UNAVAILABLE_ERROR, 213400 UNSUPPORTED_CURRENCY_PAIRS. Branch on error.type / error.code, not on the HTTP status alone. Docs (Errors): "The current limit is 500 API requests per minute." A 429 can come back as a non-JSON page ("HTML error pages such as `Cloudflare 1015 responses`"): parse error bodies defensively and back off exponentially with jitter.
open_questions: Token URL: the PHP sample of Authentication uses https://keycloak.dev-flutterwave.com/realms/flutterwave/protocol/openid-connect/token; its curl and JavaScript samples and the Multi-Environment example use https://idp.flutterwave.com/realms/flutterwave/protocol/openid-connect/token, which this spec follows.
